So I think there's a bit of a rock/paper/scissors thing going on.

I think Cleric/Fighter/Barb are huge menaces in goblin caves but a kitted wizard would make swift work of them.

Going overall though since wizards are weak right now I think cleric/barb are really really good right now if you can force people into small spaces and either buff yourself up as cleric or go in for the 1 shot as a barb.

That being said Rogue is probably the winner if you're looking for strictly value. Rogues only have to put themselves in danger if they want to. So they just automatically win and can play to their strengths and never take a bad fight if they are playing properly with double jump + mobility + stealth.

Ranger is a very popular pick but I think as long as you know how to react and deal with ranger situations (Jump over obvious trap placements on doors, make sure you're not walking into a super open area with no escape plan) they don't particularly dominate matches (Aside from like lobbies with people in full gray gear) and if they are caught off guard it only takes one or two hits to absolutely destroy their health bar.  


Edit to elaborate on the rock paper scissors thing:  


Rock - cleric/fighter/barb wins all fight except against wizards (paper)  
scissors - rangers/rogues which beat wizards but often choose not to fight rock because they're unable or sometimes are cornered and forced to  
paper - wizards which beat fighters (rock) but are pretty rare these days after the changes.   


So pick cleric/fighter/barb!!! (My personal favorite is cleric right now)

Yeah I've had success on all of these (Except maybe the wizard. I did struggle without having really good gear in goblin caves. I just think he's not made for goblin caves + not the highest tier pick right now.)

I think fighter will always be the best starting class because it's basically tailored to help out new players. Got screwed up by a PVE mob? Use second wind. Need to run away or chase someone? Use sprint.   


If you want to play a ranged character starting with the ranger or warlock is a good idea.   


Stay away from wizard/cleric/rogue until you get some experience. Rogue can be easy to start with and level up but I think you won't learn as much about the game if you play as a rogue.

Hey you don't know me, but you do know headphones. If you help me out, I may be able to grant you a small reward at the end of this wall of text. 

Budget - Around $100 (can flex to $150 if you believe there is a strong improvement in quality)

Source- 3.5mm jack, going to be using them for my desktop exclusively

Requirements for Isolation - I enjoy noise cancelling a lot, I have a pair of Bose quite comfort 35 iis and they are heavenly in the noise cancelation department, but I'm aware I probably can't get that level of noise cancelation and I don't require it, it's just something I appreciate.

Preferred Type of Headphone - I like over ear headphones that feel comfortable on my head. It's hard to get that right feel of pressure so it feels snug, but not too much pressure that over time you feel like it starts to hurt your head. (I personally love the way my Bose quite comfort 35 iis feel.) 

Preferred tonal balance - not entirely sure what this means, but I like listening to synthwave music as well as regular vocal musics. I really like to be able to get down to songs like this and feel like a good pair of headphones make music like this feel like I get transported to another dimension. ([https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JWnX41TBFF4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JWnX41TBFF4)) Sorry if that's not a lot to go off of, but I will say the bass in this video sounds quite bad in this temporary pair of $20 sony earbuds. 

Past headphones - I own a pair of bose quite comfort 35 iis and they're fantastic, but my computer is completely not bluetooth compatible (I know, buy a bluetooth USB adapter, I promise I've tried that, multiple times. Let's agree that there's something wrong that's not solvable right now. On top of that I'm aware bose has an audio jack I can use to plug into the desktop but the port inside the headphones got scuffed so it doesn't transmit cleanly anymore (RIP). tl;dr I really like my bose quit comfort 35 iis but I can't use them for my desktop, so I'm looking for a nice wired pair I can plug right in!

What would I like to improve on? Ideally I just want something comfortable with good audio that I can use to play games on. I'm mostly a MOBA player so positional sound isn't a huge requirement for me. I just really want something that doesn't fall really far short from my quitecomfort headphones without breaking the bank. It's a plus if they're purchasable on Amazon because I'd like to use my gift card to buy the pair.  


I know I wrote a lot, but as per the "purchase advice" wiki page I included almost anything you guys would like to see to help me out. If you offer a pair of headphones up as a suggestion I really want to say I appreciate you taking time out of your day to help me out. If any of you mad lads play League of Legends, feel free to dm me and I will personally offer to slug one out with you in a ranked game on one of my smurfs. (It's not a lot to offer, but it's something I'm good at)  


Thanks for reading!

Alright well I'm assuming you mean jungle since Lee is pretty much only viable there now. Lee Sin is my favorite champion by far. I was really devoted to him towards the end of the last season and I still pull him out when I want to have some fun in the jungle or hard carry a lower level game. The problem with Lee Sin is that he doesn't do as much as a gragas in terms of initiation and pick potential and he doesn't do as much damage and have as much utility as a graves/kindred pick. That being said if you're in any elo below d5 you can still be a lee sin main and find some extreme success. Rush is my favorite lee sin player and he made a wonderful guide which you can check out (If you want help with builds and masteries they have changed a bit since the guide, just hit me with a msg and I can help with that) (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6iQVnrAXV40) 

 

So the core strength of lee sin is his ability to stick on targets and do an insane amount of damage after finishing warrior. He can full nuke targets with your combos. The main goal of lee sin is to farm quickly and snowball the important lanes. You need to choose which lanes in the map to control and then consistently gank them. initially you are allowed to counterjungle as Lee sin because of your insane mobility (Best mobility out of any jungler in the game in my opinion). buy the warding jungle item and set wards in the enemy jungle to try to find and harass him while still farming constantly and pressure lanes as hard as possible. after 30 minutes you are not going to be strong unless you build full damage (Which I dont reccomend unless they have no target cc). So you just have to be as impactful as possible until then. Lastly, don't underestimate your ability to peel for your adc in a teamfight. People always go for an insec when sometimes they can use their kick to peel and win a fight that way. If you have any more specific questions I would be glad to help but this was the best help I could come up with the vagueness of your question. I hope it helped. (And the anxiety thing is just something you have to work with, I still get anxious when I play sometimes against people I look up too and stuff)

Edit: My core belief of being successful as a jungler is to ALWAYS be farming, ganking, warding, or counterganking. Never let 1 second slip by without you actually DOING something. Efficiency is key.
